texts.preamble: Dr. Anoop Bhalla (Ifs)(Retd) vs Union Of India on 25 July, 2023 Bench: Ramesh Sinha, Rajani Dubey High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur Wppil No. 61 of 2020
texts.facts: Further prayers are being made to call for protection, and safety of elephants in view of human-elephant conflict, to notify the elephant corridor and also to create a Task Force in the State. A program called "Hamar Hathi Hamar Goth" is being broadcast from All India Radio Ambikapur Station to enable the villagers to exercise caution while moving in the areas. In addition to this, Radio callers are installed on the elephants for recording their movements, so that preventive measures are being taken before the elephants enter the villages. "SAJAG" App has been introduced, which is an App based Elephant Alert System, IoT(Internet of Things) device to generate sound alert in villages using internet.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the State submits that the Forest Department, Government of Chhattisgarh has taken various measures to mitigate the human-elephant conflict and also ensures that the elephants have a good natural habitat with sufficient sources of food and water. It is submitted that Government of Chhattisgarh and its Forest Department is committed to protecting the wildlife and management of the elephants as well. To lessen the problem of human-elephant conflict, Forest Department is taking various initiatives to educate the masses as to how to deal with wild elephants. Every endeavour is being made to protect and preserve the elephants in accordance with law. It is further categorically submitted by the State that Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun and the State have jointly initiated the project named "Conservation, Management of Elephants in Chhattisgarh: Capacity Dr. Anoop Bhalla (Ifs)(Retd) vs Union Of India on 25 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27585897/ 2 Building Initiative On the Dispersal and Ranging Patterns for Effective Management of Human Elephant Interaction". This project was initiated in the year 2017 for suggesting various measures for conservation and protection of elephants and to reduce elephant-human conflicts. Sincere steps are being initiated by the State to reduce human-elephant conflicts and to provide better management and conservation methods for not only the elephants but also other wild animals. Lastly, learned counsel submits that petitioners' reliefs have been adequately redressed/executed by the respondent/State authorities, as detailed in their reply dated 20.10.2020. Wppil 61 of 2020 4. Learned counsel for respondents-6 and 7 fairly submits that various reliefs prayed for by the petitioners have been adequately redressed and answered by these respondents, as detailed in their reply dated 10.01.2021. It is submitted that CSPDCL (Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Company Limited) is working strictly as per the standards prescribed in the Regulation 58 of the Central Electricity Authority (Measure relating to Safety and Electric Supply )Regulations, 2010. It never flouted the prescription of standards/height/clearance for erecting electrical lines. CSPDCL being concerned with the human-elephant conflict in the State, has been working rather rigorously in conforming to the directions issued by this Hon'ble Court order dated 12.03.2019. Regular inspections of electricity connections are being conducted in the affected areas and instituted theft cases.
